title: Modules: import and export
learningObjectives: Explain modules: import and export and debug or organise JavaScript code using the concept.

understand.concept: JavaScript modules split code into separate files. export exposes selected bindings; import brings them into another module. Modules have their own scope, run in strict mode, and are loaded with type=module in browsers. Static imports are resolved before module evaluation.
understand.whyItMatters: Modules help organise larger applications and define explicit dependencies. Avoid circular dependencies and keep module responsibilities clear.
understand.analogy: A module is a labelled toolbox that exports the tools other parts of the application are allowed to use.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; debugger, module, prototype, and function-call behaviour follow JavaScript and browser runtime rules.

explain.narrative: The script is loaded as a module. A multi-file project would export the greeting function from one module and import it into another.

examples.explanation: The script is loaded as a module. A multi-file project would export the greeting function from one module and import it into another.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page demonstrates the code organisation or runtime behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create math.js with an exported function and main.js that imports it. Load main.js using type=module.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example that uses the feature. Inspect its runtime behaviour and explain the scope, receiver, or call path involved.
hints: Use breakpoints to inspect changing values.
Test methods both through their object and when passed as callbacks.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Modules: import and export</title></head><body>
<script type='module'>const greeting=(name)=>`Hello, ${name}`;document.body.insertAdjacentText('beforeend',greeting('Learner'));</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which keyword exposes a binding from a JavaScript module?
questions.explanation: export makes a binding available for import by other modules.

questions.prompt: What is a useful debugging or architecture practice?
options: Inspect actual runtime behaviour and keep dependencies explicit
Assume the code behaves as intended
questions.answer: Inspect actual runtime behaviour and keep dependencies explicit
questions.explanation: Reliable debugging and modular design depend on understanding actual execution and dependencies.
